content_log_investigation.goal: Identify a stable callable function that writes entries visible in Settings -> Creator -> Content Log, so the SDK logger and ScriptClient LogSink can hook the game's own path.

findings.note: Confirms the in-game viewer is backed by a ContentLog store/file; this is the acceptance surface.

findings.evidence: CONTENT_LOG_FILE / CONTENT_LOG_GUI / CONTENT_LOG_GUI_LEVEL / CONTENT_LOG_GUI_SHOW_ON_ERRORS at rdata 0xf298b0e..0xf298b45; options.content_log_file_enabled / options.content_log_gui_enabled
findings.note: Shows a configurable Content Log file and GUI filter; the debug/OutputDebugString sink is a different, non-GUI surface.

findings.evidence: BedrockLog::LogDetails::createLog RTTI lambda type in .data; Bedrock::ResultLogger::log(LogLevel, LogArea, const std::string&, const CallStack&) __FUNCSIG__ at rdata 0xf830f69; Bedrock::LogOrAssertLevel / Bedrock::LogArea parameter types; ContentLog::ThreadSpecificData inside Bedrock::Threading::InstancedThreadLocal RTTI at .data 0x123241e0
findings.note: The game has a structured BedrockLog/ContentLog logger with level+area parameters. No callable RVA was recovered: the release EXE has no PDB, Ghidra auto-analysis of the 327MB image times out, and the ContentLog strings are pooled with zero direct xrefs.

findings.evidence: RVA 0x886b530..0x886d523 reads all three menu.creator.contentLog strings (lea at 0x886c0d3 / 0x886c7e6 / 0x886ce81); supplied by Muse 2026-11-20
findings.note: This is the GUI reader side, NOT the write function. Follow its store access to reach the writer in a future live/PDB-assisted round.

findings.evidence: RVA 0x3B13E0; entry bytes 56 57 53 48 81 EC 80 00 00 00 4C 89 C7 80 79 02 00; the ResultLogger::log FUNCSIG string (rdata 0xf830f69) has exactly one code xref, inside this function. ABI: void __fastcall(const LevelWrap*, const AreaWrap*, const std::string&); defaults level=2 / area=45 when hasValue=0. Muse RE 2026-11-23 (contentlog-re-20261123.md).
findings.note: This is the single dispatch funnel of the game's public log API. Its only caller is the queue drain FUN_1403b1260; the front-end FUN_1403b1130 (83 callsites) and fmt front-end FUN_1403b1570 converge to it, so every game log entry passes through here.

findings.evidence: Global pair at VA 0x1528CD388 read live as null at every probe round (BOL 2026-11-23, rounds 1-3, UI on and off, in-world). A full .text RIP-relative scan finds 5 reference sites, all inside the funnel/drain cluster; the only write (RVA 0x3B1517, movups of a zeroed xmm) CLEARS the pair. No direct installer exists in .text.
findings.note: F's path 1 (installed-handler dispatch, the GUI history feed) is inert in this retail build/session type; the installer is presumably an editor/dev-side hookup or an indirect registration not present here.

findings.evidence: BOL probe rounds 1-3 (2026-11-23): 212 dispatches through the funnel — areas 0..52 x levels {2, 258} x 2 rounds, plus targeted (level, area) sets at area 45 with levels {1,2,4,258} — all executed cleanly (0 faults). Zero entries appeared in the Content Log GUI history (checked with UI ON, level Verbose, scrolled) or in any file under the Wine prefix (full-tree grep; no ContentLog file created/modified in-session; 506 historical files from the game's content-loading pipeline untouched).
findings.note: F's path 2 (BedrockLog core emit when level & 0x100) also reaches no active sink in a normal gameplay session. Conclusion: on 1.26.65.1 retail, funnel-dispatched entries have no reachable surface; the historical ContentLog*.txt files are produced by the game's content-loading pipeline, a different producer. The SDK wiring stays fail-closed: the symbol is candidate, calls are entry-checked and SEH-guarded, file/debug logging is unaffected, and the route activates automatically wherever the game does install its handler.

symbol_to_add_when_resolved.name: ContentLog::write
symbol_to_add_when_resolved.expected_shape: void __fastcall(level, area, message) or void __fastcall(message, level, area); the adapter selects via the optional 'call' field ('level_area_message' default, or 'message_level_area')
symbol_to_add_when_resolved.status_policy: candidate until exact-build entry guard + ABI are verified; runtime_verified false until a live BOL observation

content_log_investigation.runtime_behavior: The symbol is added as candidate with call shape 'level_area_stringref' (classes/ContentLog.json). The adapter resolves it under the exact-build entry guard, installs the writer, and dispatches through the funnel under SEH; on builds where the symbol is absent it fails closed exactly as before (one OutputDebugString line, file/debug logs kept). File logging is independent of the native writer and was verified unaffected in-session. Live surfacing in the Creator Content Log is negative on 1.26.65.1 retail sessions (see surfacing-negative-exhaustive) — a property of the game's build, not of the call.
